newsitem.title: UK: Norwich Union shareholders approve float.
newsitem.headline: Norwich Union shareholders approve float.

text.p: Members of the Norwich Union, Britain's third-largest life insurer, on Friday voted overwhelmingly in favour of plans to float on the London Stock Exchange on Friday.

Results of postal voting showed a 98.9 percent majority in favour of the scheme. The official result will not be announced until next Tuesday after votes at an extraordinary general meeting, where around 200 members attended, are included.

The demutualisation and flotation of the company, the first by a mutually-owned British insurer, will value it at around five billion pounds ($8.2 billion) and rank Norwich among Britain's 50 largest companies.
The company needecd the backing of three quarters of those who voted. Some 1,850,673 postal votes were in favour, with 21,145 against, Norwich Union said.

Almost two million members will receive shares worth an average of 800 pounds, and another one million "non-profit' members of the group will receive a fixed handout of shares worth beween 330 and 400 pounds on the group's flotation in une.
Norwich Union's 10,000 employees will share in the giveawy, receiving 150 shares each. The share handout will be worth a total of around 3.1 billion pounds.
The two million with-profit members will receive a minimum of 300 shares, and additional shares based on the value and duration of their policy holdings as at October 1, 1996.
